chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام:
Regarding a man upon whom a hadd punishment became due, but it was not carried out on him until he became mentally disturbed, so he said:
If he had made the hadd binding upon himself while he was sound and had no affliction involving loss of intellect, the hadd is to be carried out on him, whatever the case may be.

key_terms.أَوْجَبَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ الْحَدَّ: He established the hadd against himself, meaning by valid self-confession.
key_terms.أُقِيمَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَدُّ: The hadd is carried out upon him.
key_terms.حَدٌّ: A fixed legal punishment in Islamic law.
key_terms.ذَهَابِ عَقْلٍ: Loss of intellect or mental capacity.
key_terms.صَحِيحٌ: Sound and medically or mentally well at the time in question.

ai.seo_question: Is a hadd punishment still carried out if a person becomes mentally disturbed after confessing while sane?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a hadd punishment in the case of later mental disturbance. If the person had established the hadd against himself while mentally sound and free of any loss of reason, the punishment remains enforceable even after that later condition arises.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5046 - In the narration reported by Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Riʾab from Abu Ubaydah from Abu Jafar (as),
regarding a man upon whom a legal punishment (hadd) was due but he was not punished until he became mentally disturbed.
Imam (as) said: "If he had confessed to the hadd upon himself while he was sound in mind and free from any mental illness, then the hadd must be carried out on him regardless of his current state."
